title: Coins and notes
summary: Get to know coins and notes, make an amount of money in different ways, and see that more coins is not always more money.
guide: In the UK we use pounds (£) and pence (p). 100p make £1. Every {{term:coin}} and {{term:banknote}} shows how much it is worth.
Ten 1p coins are worth the same as one 10p coin. Ten 10p coins are worth the same as £1. Just like ones, tens and hundreds!
The number of coins doesn't matter. What they are worth matters. One coin can be worth more than lots of coins.
To make an amount, start with the biggest coin that fits, then see how much is left.
Tap the coins at the bottom to put them in the purse. Tap a coin in the purse to take it out.

same-money.title: Which is more?
same-money.prompt: Ali has ten 1p coins. Sara has one 10p coin. Who has more money?
same-money.hint: Count Ali's 1p coins: 1, 2, 3 … 10. How many pence is that?
same-money.why: Ali has 10 coins and Sara has 1. Why do they have the same money?
same-money.model: Ten 1p coins make 10p altogether. Sara's coin is 10p too. The number of coins doesn't matter; what they are worth does.

feedback.counted-pieces: Ali has more coins. But does he have more money? Count his coins.
feedback.wrong: Sara's coin is 10p. Count Ali's coins.

make-amount.title: Make 35p
make-amount.hint: Try a 20p, then a 10p. How much more do you need?
make-amount.why: Could you make 35p with different coins? Tell one more way.
make-amount.model: Yes. For example 20p + 10p + 5p, or seven 5p coins, or 10p + 10p + 10p + 5p. The same amount can be made in lots of ways.

feedback.too-big: Too much. Take a coin out and count again.
feedback.empty: Tap the coins at the bottom to put them in the purse.

fewest.title: As few coins as possible
fewest.prompt: Put 70p in the purse. Use as few coins as you can!
fewest.hint: Start with the biggest coin that is not more than 70p. Then see how much is left.
fewest.why: How did you know the fewest coins you could use?
fewest.model: I started with the biggest coin that fits: 50p. That left 20p, and there is a 20p coin. Bigger coins mean fewer coins.

feedback.not-fewest: That is 70p, well done! But you can make it with fewer coins. Try bigger coins.
feedback.too-big: Too much. Take a coin out.
feedback.empty: Tap the coins at the bottom to put them in the purse.

more-money.title: More coins, more money?
more-money.prompt: Reza has 5 coins. Zahra has 2 coins. Who has more money?
more-money.hint: Count Reza's coins in tens: 10, 20, 30 … Then add up Zahra's coins.
more-money.success: Right! Zahra has 70p and Reza has only 50p.
more-money.why: Reza has more coins. So why does Zahra have more money?
more-money.model: Five 10p coins make 50p. Zahra's 50p and 20p make 70p, which is more. To compare money, count what the coins are worth, not how many there are.

feedback.counted-pieces: Reza has more coins. But count them: how much money is it?
feedback.not-equal: They are not the same. Compare 50p with 50p + 20p.
feedback.wrong: Count how much each group is worth, then compare.
